title: Customization and the Rewards Benefit
lessons: The player first engages with Starbucks through the unusually customizable drink order itself.
The player is already in Starbucks Rewards and sees a monthly benefit that covers one drink customization up to the program limit.

text: Corner cafe. The person ahead of you is on their fifth modifier and the barista hasn't blinked. You start rehearsing yours.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: At what point does my order become embarrassing?

entry-first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Around the third modifier. I'll still make it, and I'll still write a name on the cup, correct or not.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: You encourage this.

entry-first-4.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: I do. Milk, syrup, foam, temperature, shots, the name on the side. Some of it costs extra. I'd rather you leave with your drink than with a number.

choice-first.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: You're up. Go on.

choices.text: I like being called by name, even a slightly mangled one.
Too many options makes ordering feel like work, and a wrong name makes it worse.
I'd rather a coffee shop tell me what it makes well and skip the theater around my name.

first-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then the name's part of the drink for you. I'll try to get it right. I'll get it close.

first-1-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Just get it right most of the time.

first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Fair. A wrong name undoes more than a right one builds. Keep it simple, then. Nobody's grading you at the counter.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Tall coffee.

first-2-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Beautifully legible. I might even spell your name right.

first-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: That's a different kind of coffee place, and I get the appeal of skipping the show. I'm the show. It's what I've got.
Monday. The app has a badge on it: one drink customization free this month, up to the program limit.

entry-return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: One customization is on me this month.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You mean the thing I already pay extra for?

entry-return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Within the Mod Monday limit, yes.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: So my existing habit became a loyalty perk.

entry-return-5.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: I know what you like. I might as well reward the expensive part.

choice-return.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Oat milk, then? Same as always?

choices.text: I was going to add it anyway, so that's useful.
A free modification is tiny compared with what I spend here.
I don't want a reward system nudging me to decorate every drink.

return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: That's when a small perk feels real. When it lands on something you were doing anyway.

return-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: It's small. I'm not going to call two dollars life-changing. It's a way of saying I noticed, at a price I can afford to say it every month.

return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then order it plain. A reward shouldn't invent a need. If it did that to you, tell me, I'd rather know.
